newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mostly higher after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mostly higher after choppy session.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled mostly higher after a choppy, directionless session, traders said.

Traders said commercial buying supported KCBT wheat, with Cargill Investor Services said to have bought two million Sept bushels. CIS also bull-spread 1.5 million July/Sept bushels at two to 3-1/2 cents.

Traders said there was very little fundamental news in wheat, and that the market was volatile at times because of changing weather forecasts for dry corn- and soy-growing areas of the Midwest, traders said.

"It's been a slow, directionless day -- real choppy. We've been looking to (CBOT) corn and beans for direction. At times, it would look like they were ready to (drop) but then they'd stop and turn on a dime," a KCBT trader said.
KCBT wheat also saw some early spillover strength from MGE spring wheat, which rallied on fund- and mill-related buying.
KCBT wheat settled one cent per bushel lower to 2-1/2 cents higher, with September up 2-1/2 cents at $3.43-1/2.
Traders said Shay Grain bear-spread 1.8 million Sept/July bushels at two to three cents.
Thursday's volume was estimated at 42.39 million bushels -- the lightest so far this week.
